sections.title: Three more owners
sections.content: There are three more owners: 'our', 'your' when you speak to several people, and 'their'. The endings are *-nk*, *-tok / -tek* and *-uk / -ük*. For one person you say *szobád*; for several you say *szobátok*. After a consonant a linking vowel comes first and follows vowel harmony: *barát* → *barátunk*, *barátotok*.

sections.title: Their: the j belongs to the suffix
sections.content: 'Their' follows the 3rd person singular. A word that takes *-ja / -je* takes *-juk / -jük*: *szobája* → *szobájuk*, *barátja* → *barátjuk*. A word that takes *-a / -e* takes *-uk / -ük*: *kulcsa* → *kulcsuk*, *könyve* → *könyvük*. *szoba* lengthens its last vowel (*szobánk*), and *név* gets shorter (*nevünk*, not *névünk*): learn such words one by one.
Small letters change the owner: *barátunk* is our friend, *barátjuk* is their friend. And *szobád* is for one person, *szobátok* for several: English *your* can't show that, Hungarian always does.
